 Bruins vs. Wild PREVIEW: Boston looks to rebound against Minnesota
 by Skyler W. Nov 14, 2026, 11:30 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just the Facts
 The Time: 7pm EST 
 The Place: TD Garden, Boston, Massachusetts 
 Place to Watch: NESN, MINNHL, Wild+ 
 Place to Listen: 98.5 The Sports Hub 
 Game Preview
 There are two things you must know about the Minnesota Wild.
 First, they are pretty good. Just all around.
 The Wild are tied with the Canes in points, they lead the Central Division and Western Conference, they just pantsed the Leafs and got an OT winner against Montreal, and played a VERY tight game against the Lightning and eventually got a point out of that one. They’re comfortably in the top ten of most possession metrics that matter, and have an embarrassment of riches at just about every position; Kaprizov, Boldy, the Haunted Hughes, Joel Eriksson EK, Wallstedt…They even have both Folignos. Just by showing up, the Wild represent a major hurdle for the Bruins to overcome just because of who they are.
 Second, they are hurt.
 They’ve only got three guys on the mend, but living life without those three guys hurts. Joel Eriksson Ek was their 1C that has largely traded his previous year selke bonafides for just hammering the puck up the ice and giving Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy all the help they need to be certified nightmares to face. He’s day-to-day after getting hurt on Thursday. Without him, their center depth absolutely craters. Their best goalie; Jesper Wallstedt, has a .925 SV% and a 13-2-3. He’s out with a hip injury with no real timetable of return beyond “a month”; he’ll travel today but it’s unlikely he plays. In his place is Calvin Pickard, who is…not Jesper Wallstedt.
 The B’s need to take advantage of Pickard’s preference to give up less than 90% of the shots he faces, and especially crack the Wild’s net-front D, which so far this season has been quite formidable. They also absolutely need to cut down on the dumb, unforced penalties, as the Wild are a nasty team on the power play.
 Can they find a groove and Re-Mild the Wild? Let’s find out together!
